title: Sections over a finite separable field extension are stalk invariants
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension], $K^{\rm sep}$ a separable closure [def-kun-separably-closed] embedded in an algebraic closure $\Omega$, $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\rm sep}/K)$ with its Krull topology, and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ the geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $\operatorname{Spec}K$, with stalk $M=F_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and the action of $G$ induced by changing the lifts in pointed etale neighbourhoods. For each finite separable intermediate field $K\subseteq L\subseteq K^{\rm sep}$, put $H_L=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\rm sep}/L)$. Restriction to the chosen lift of $\bar s$ gives a bijection $F(\operatorname{Spec}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}M^{H_L}$. These bijections are natural in morphisms of sheaves and in all $K$-embeddings $j:L\to L'$ between such fields: if $\sigma\in G$ restricts to $j$ on $L$, then pullback of sections along $\operatorname{Spec}L'\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ corresponds to $m\mapsto\sigma\cdot m$ from $M^{H_L}$ to $M^{H_{L'}}$. This does not depend on the choice of $\sigma$.

proof.text: For a finite Galois extension $E/L$ with group $Q$, an etale $\operatorname{Spec}L$-scheme is an etale $\operatorname{Spec}K$-scheme by composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]; coverings in $(\operatorname{Spec}L)_{\mathrm{et}}$ are coverings in $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Thus $V\mapsto F(V)$ is a sheaf on $(\operatorname{Spec}L)_{\mathrm{et}}$ with the same sections, and [lem-exc-finite-galois-sections-descent] identifies $F(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ with the $Q$-invariant sections over $E$.

source.place: Tag 04JM, Lemma lemma-global-sections-point, direct proof after the formal proof

proof.text: Passing through the filtered-colimit definition of the geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], shrink an etale neighbourhood to the connected open containing the image of the lift. With $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $X=U$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] says this open is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a finite separable extension embedded in $K^{\rm sep}$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] enlarges it to a finite Galois $E/L$. The germ map $F(\operatorname{Spec}E)\to M$ is injective: the index category is cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], and every morphism of pointed neighbourhoods $(U',\bar u')\to(\operatorname{Spec}E,\bar e)$ is etale and surjective (the target has one point and $U'$ is nonempty), hence a covering; restriction is injective by the sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. For $q\in Q=\operatorname{Gal}(E/L)$, lift $q$ to $\tau\in H_L$; the germ of $q^*t$ at the chosen lift is the germ of $t$ at the lift moved by $\tau$, namely $\tau\cdot m=m$, so $q^*t=t$ by injectivity. Hence an $H_L$-invariant stalk element is represented by a $Q$-invariant section and finite Galois descent gives a unique section over $L$. Conversely, restriction of a section over $L$ is fixed by $H_L$. This proves the bijection with $M^{H_L}$.

source.place: Tag 04JM, Lemma lemma-global-sections-point, direct proof after the formal proof

proof.text: For a $K$-embedding $j:L\to L'$ and an extension $\sigma\in G$ of $j$, pullback of sections is restriction along $\operatorname{Spec}L'\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. The naturality in the representing object from [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] and the action on geometric stalks from [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] show that the germ of the pulled-back section at the chosen lift of $L'$ is $\sigma\cdot m$ when the original germ is $m\in M^{H_L}$. Since $\sigma(L)=j(L)\subseteq L'$, we have $\sigma^{-1}H_{L'}\sigma\subseteq H_L$, so for $h\in H_{L'}$, $h\sigma m=\sigma(\sigma^{-1}h\sigma)m=\sigma m$; hence $\sigma m\in M^{H_{L'}}$. The formula is compatible with composition.

If $\sigma'$ is another extension of $j$, then $\sigma'^{-1}\sigma$ fixes $L$, hence belongs to $H_L$; therefore $\sigma'\cdot m=\sigma\cdot m$ for $m\in M^{H_L}$. Naturality in a morphism of sheaves follows from the naturality in the presheaf of the Yoneda bijection and functoriality of stalks.
